skill.name: whatsapp-closer
skill.description: Improve WhatsApp sales conversations with qualification rules, Spanish scripts, objection handling, follow-up guidance, and conversion metrics.
skill.summary: Draft and review WhatsApp sales scripts with confirmed business details, limited follow-ups, and human handoff.
skill.author: rabbitdesigns22

security_audit.summary: Both system reconnaissance flags are false positives: they describe prohibited messaging behavior and sales performance metrics. No evidence found of system inspection, credential access, unauthorized data transfer, or prompt injection in the reviewed source. The skill provides prose guidance and scripts, not executable integrations.

static_findings.snippet: - Free-form messages outside the 24 h window (templates only); messaging people who said stop; spam
Time to first reply (<5 min) · reply rate to the first message · qualified / conversations · booked

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 50 appears under the Never heading and prohibits spam, unwanted messages, and free-form messages outside the permitted window. It contains no system inspection instructions or commands.
Line 58 lists sales metrics such as response time, booking rates, and cost per sale. These are business performance measures, not host reconnaissance or sensitive system discovery.

content.value_statement: Ad leads can stop responding when chat replies hide prices, ask too many questions, or lack a clear next step. This skill provides sales scripts, objection responses, and review methods for improving WhatsApp conversations.
actual_capabilities: Draft formal and informal Spanish replies for leads arriving from advertisements.
Structure qualification and price responses around confirmed business information.
Adapt objection responses and recommend one option with a concrete next step.
Plan two or three follow-ups with messaging-window restrictions and stop conditions.
Review conversations using response, qualification, booking, attendance, and payment metrics.
Guide incremental assistant changes through simulations, before-and-after tests, and rollback criteria.
limitations: Provides instructions and sample scripts, not a WhatsApp connection, message sender, booking system, or payment processor.
Does not verify current Meta pricing, messaging rules, or template approval requirements.
Cited evidence includes sales calls and email studies, not only WhatsApp research; conversion improvements are not guaranteed.
Requires confirmed prices, availability, testimonials, and conversation data from the business.

use_cases.title: Respond to Advertisement Leads
use_cases.description: Prepare short Spanish replies that continue the advertisement offer, qualify the request, and propose a visit or call.

use_cases.title: Standardize Sales Follow-Ups
use_cases.description: Create consistent objection responses and limited follow-up sequences while respecting opt-outs and offering human assistance.

use_cases.title: Review Assistant Conversion Gaps
use_cases.description: Inspect conversation drop-offs, propose one prompt change, and define simulations and metrics before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Write a First Reply
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a short, formal Spanish WhatsApp reply for [business]. The lead clicked an ad for [offer] and wrote 'Hi, info'. Ask whether they need [option A] or [option B]. Use only the supplied facts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: respond to a new advertisement lead.

prompt_templates.title: Answer Price and Objections
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft informal Spanish responses to 'How much?' and 'Too expensive' for [service]. Use confirmed starting price [price] and pricing factors [factors]. Ask one relevant question per response. Do not invent discounts, guarantees, or availability.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: adapt responses to common buying concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Limited Follow-Ups
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan three Spanish follow-ups for [service], around days one, three, and seven. Last customer message: [timestamp]. Approved templates: [list]. Mark any step needing an approved template; do not treat draft wording as approved. Stop on opt-out and offer human assistance. Use only confirmed details: [facts].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a follow-up plan for human review.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Live Sales Assistant
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these 20-30 anonymized conversations: [conversations]. Current prompt: [prompt]. Baseline metrics: [metrics]. Identify the main drop-off and propose one targeted change. Define a failing-before, passing-after test and ten conversation simulations. Set review points after one and two weeks, with rollback if bookings per conversation decline.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: test a focused improvement before changing a live assistant.

output_examples.input: Adapt a price-first reply for cleaning services. Confirmed starting price: $80. Final price depends on property size.
output_examples.output: Our cleaning service starts at $80. The final price depends on the property size. Could you share the size or send a photo?

output_examples.input: A customer says the quote is too expensive. Draft a short response without offering an immediate discount.
output_examples.output: I understand. Are you comparing this with another quote or with the budget you had in mind?

output_examples.input: Recommend one booking step after qualification. The business confirmed Tuesday at 10 and Thursday at 3 are available.
output_examples.output: Based on what you shared, I recommend an assessment visit. Would Tuesday at 10 or Thursday at 3 work better?

best_practices: Provide confirmed prices, service details, availability, and genuine proof before generating scripts.
Verify current Meta rules and template requirements; honor opt-outs and keep human assistance available.
Review anonymized conversations, test one change at a time, and compare booking rates against your own baseline.
anti_patterns: Inventing prices, testimonials, guarantees, deadlines, or reserved appointments to create pressure.
Sending repeated unsolicited messages, ignoring opt-outs, or treating draft follow-ups as approved templates.
Deploying multiple untested prompt changes or judging success only by conversation volume.

faq.question: Does this skill send WhatsApp messages?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and draft scripts. Sending messages requires a separate WhatsApp setup and appropriate authorization.

faq.question: Which languages do the supplied scripts use?
faq.answer: The source includes Spanish examples with formal and informal wording. Adapt the language and tone to the customer.

faq.question: Can it set prices or promise appointments?
faq.answer: No. Supply confirmed prices and availability. The skill explicitly warns against inventing business claims or deadlines.

faq.question: Does it guarantee more sales?
faq.answer: No. Its evidence includes other sales channels and opinion-based methods. Measure results against your own baseline.

faq.question: Are the WhatsApp policy details guaranteed current?
faq.answer: No. Check current Meta documentation for messaging windows, pricing, and approved templates before using the guidance.

faq.question: How should I test changes to an existing assistant?
faq.answer: Review 20-30 conversations, change one behavior, simulate ten scenarios, and compare results after one and two weeks. Roll back if booking rates decline.
